data.name: Ciprian
data.gender_notes: Ciprian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'ciprianus', meaning 'god's helper'. In early Christianity, Ciprian was a Roman soldier martyred during the persecutions under Emperor Decius in the 3rd century AD. The name Ciprian carries the meaning “God's helper” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ciprian usually hope their child will grow to embody god's helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ciprian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ciprian total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ciprian, derived from the Latin word 'ciprianus', holds significance as a Roman name that became popular within the Christian community due to the martyrdom of Saint Ciprian, a soldier martyred during the Roman Emperor Decius' persecutions in the 3rd century AD. The name is a reminder of the bravery and sacrifice of early Christian martyrs, and has been passed down through generations as a symbol of courage and faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ciprian carries strong spiritual significance as it is derived from the Latin word 'ciprianus', meaning 'god's helper'. The name reflects the belief in the presence and power of God in one's life, and the desire to be of service to Him. The name also serves as a reminder of the important historical figure, Saint Ciprian, who remained steadfast in his faith even in the face of persecution, offering inspiration and encouragement for those facing religious or personal challenges in their own lives.
